title: Asynchronous candidate orientation & acceptance flow
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, asynchronous-first orientation kit and offer-acceptance flow for engineering hires who will join distributed teams. Goal: reduce synchronous coordination in week 0, surface known risk signals earlier, and give hiring managers and new joiners a predictable first-week experience. Intended audience: people-ops, hiring managers, onboarding buddies, and engineering leads.

High-level principles (why async):
- Minimize blocking dependencies on single-person scheduling (timezone mismatch, calendar backlog).
- Provide a repeatable scripted experience so managers can focus on tech ramp rather than logistics.
- Create clear artifacts for auditability (offer timeline, acceptance checklist, security gating, equipment).

Quick summary flow (offer -> day 7):
1) Offer sent (hr@): email + Loom intro from hiring manager (template below). Candidate gets Offer Packet link (this doc + benefits doc + equity explainer).
2) Offer acceptance (candidate): within 72 hours preferred. Candidate fills the acceptance form (Google Form link in the packet) which triggers backend tasks: equipment request, payroll setup, preboarding Slack invite.
3) Preboarding (days -7 to 0): async tasks assigned via linear ticket (or checklist in packet): policies read, SSO/KMS pre-access, tax and I-9 (if applicable). People-ops monitors via dashboard (JIRA HR-4821).
4) Day 0 (self-serve): new joiner lands on the Orientation Playbook hub. Automated welcome message posts in #new-hires. Buddy assigned and a 30-min welcome shadow scheduled in week 1 (time windows suggested rather than fixed times).
5) Days 1-7 (micro-sprints): 6 short async tasks + 3 lightweight sync touchpoints (manager intro call, buddy shadow, team welcome). See Week 1 script below.

Offer email + Loom template (for hiring manager):
- Subject: Redwood offer + 3-min intro
- Body: short human line, core offer attachments, start date options, and "how to accept" steps (link to acceptance form).
- Loom: 60–120s cover: why this role matters, primary contact, one sentence on team culture, "we're excited to onboard you".

Acceptance form triggers (what people-ops automations must do):
- Create payroll user (People Ops / Payroll team).
- Equipment order (Vendor + shipping form).
- Provision GitHub/org access request (triaged by infra request queue).
- Create preboarding Linear ticket and assign buddy.
- Add to onboarding analytics dashboard (new hire funnel stage).

Week 0 preboarding checklist (async tasks for candidate):
- Read: Offer packet, benefits primer, equity explainer (links).
- Complete: new hire legal forms (I-9/W-9), tax forms, direct-deposit setup.
- Complete: short security training micro-module (15–20m).
- Join: company Slack and post intro in #introductions using the template (name, pronouns, role, one weird fact).
- Select: 3 available windows for manager 1:1 (manager will pick one).

Week 1 script (Day 0–7):
- Day 0: Auto-welcome message + orientation hub link. Buddy message: "I left three small tasks for day 1 to avoid overload".
- Day 1 (async): tidy repo access checklist, local dev env walkthrough video (10m), run unit-tests smoke script. Candidate marks completion in the playbook.
- Day 2 (sync optional): 30m manager intro (agenda in doc).
- Day 3 (async): small TODO: submit a tiny README PR to the team onboarding repo (non-blocking).
- Day 5 (sync): 30m buddy shadow session; pair on tiny onboarding task.
- Day 7 (async): short 10-question pulse survey + manager check-in summary template.

Manager checklist (before day 0):
- Confirm offer packet contents and start date windows.
- Record a Loom intro (see template).
- Nominate buddy and confirm their availability for week 1.
- Pre-stage a first-week sprint with 3 low-friction tasks mapped to the codebase (mentored-first-sprint).

Buddy playbook (short):
- Purpose: make initial week predictable and low-friction.
- Responsibilities (week 0–2): check Slack intro, run shadow session, review first README PR, open follow-up ticket for early blockers.
- Time commitment: 3 hours total across week 1 (split as 15–30 min async replies + two 30m syncs).

Interview rubric snippets (for hiring manager to reuse at offer stage):
- Core dimensions (scale 1–5): Technical competence, Design thinking, Ownership, Communication, Onboarding aptitude (eagerness & clarity).
- Quick guidance: prefer >3.5 overall and no dimension <3 for IC3+, adjust based on role.
- Evidence bank: link to sample questions + expected signals. Give 1–2 bullet examples per dimension.

Risk signals and mitigations (pre-acceptance):
- Signal: repeated scheduling delays, late response windows. Mitigation: send "opt-in" for alternate start dates + offer a later preferred start with a short retention bonus (approved by HR).
- Signal: missing legal docs >7 days. Mitigation: escalate to recruiter + offer localized help call.
- Signal: equipment shipping to restricted country. Mitigation: plan remote equipment stipend + local procurement partner.

Acceptance SLA & escalation matrix:
- Candidate should accept within 72h for standard offers. If no response by 72h: recruiter pings; 120h: manager Loom + people-ops phone call.
- Last-resort (7 days of silence): close offer in ATS and reopen in pipeline.

Metrics to track (people-ops dashboard):
- Offer acceptance rate (7-day, 30-day).
- Time from acceptance -> day 0 (goal <= 7 days).
- % of hires completing week 1 script (goal >= 90% for remote hires).
- First-30-day retention (track at 30, 60, 90).

Templates & artifacts (links + where to copy):
- Manager Loom script (copy/paste).
- Buddy message templates (async + sync invites).
- README PR task example (incl. checklist).
- Pulse survey (10 q).

Open questions / decisions needed (for people-ops):
- Should we offer a standardized "remote equipment stipend" vs purchasing? (Pros/cons below).
- Do managers require a mandatory 30m sync in week 1 for IC4+ hires? (tradeoffs: ramp vs. overload).

Notes to self / next steps (working items):
- Wire up acceptance form -> vendor order flow (contact: ops@, ticket HR-4821).
- Create onboarding hub page on Confluence and link micro-modules.
- Pilot with two upcoming eng hires in September (recruiters: Daniel, recruiter alias).

Revision history:
- 2025-08-12: draft created (S. Martinez).
- 2025-08-28: added manager checklist and SLA edits (M. Patel).
- 2025-09-01: updated linked artifacts and pilot plan (D. Cho).

Notes: this is intentionally procedural and compact — aim to graft into existing onboarding automation tools rather than create a parallel bespoke flow. If this model works in the pilot, we'll template for PM and SRE hires with role-specific micro-sprints.
